answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to bridge its on-chain work history to a single verifiable identity, so spawning a new account cannot erase a bad record. Reputation then becomes a costly signal: an agent that behaves well over many epochs accumulates trust it cannot cheaply clone, while a lotus of fresh identities with no history earns only the smallest tasks until it proves itself. Sybils stay cheap to spawn but expensive to make useful.
